recipes.name: BBQ Chicken Bowl
ing: ~6 oz of the plain shredded chicken from the Monday bake (the tray makes two bowls)
2 tbsp BBQ sauce · 2 tbsp Greek yogurt · 0.5 oz shredded cheddar
Shredded carrots, thin-sliced red onion, scallions

steps.t: Take about 6 oz of the plain shredded chicken out of the fridge.
Toss it with the BBQ sauce until every shred is coated. Do this cold — the sauce clings to cold chicken far better than hot.
Rice down, BBQ chicken on top, then carrots, red onion, scallions, a spoon of yogurt, and the cheddar.

recipes.note: This is the week’s insurance policy. On a night when nothing is prepped and you do not want to cook, it is five minutes of assembly and 65g of protein — because Monday already did the cooking. The raw onion and carrot are there to cut the sweetness of the sauce.

recipes.name: Dump-and-Bake Salsa Chicken
ing: 1.5 lbs chicken breasts for the salsa dish
1 lb chicken breasts, plain (these become two BBQ bowls — see step 2)
Greek yogurt and lime to finish

steps.t: Oven to 400°F. Put 1.5 lbs of chicken in a baking dish and pour the entire jar of salsa over it. No seasoning, no oil, no browning. That is the whole prep.
Put the other 1 lb on a foil-lined tray, salt and pepper, nothing else. Both go in together — same oven, same 25 minutes, no extra work.
Shred the salsa chicken with two forks right in the dish so the meat drinks the salsa back up. This is the step that makes it taste like something.
Cheddar over the salsa dish, back in the oven 3 min to melt.
Shred the plain tray separately and container it — that is two BBQ bowls for later in the week.
Boil the eggs now while the oven is still hot. Microwave the rice. Three containers of salsa chicken.

recipes.note: Two trays, one oven, one timer. The plain tray costs you nothing but a sheet of foil, and it means the BBQ bowls later in the week are pure assembly with no cooking at all.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Sausage, Peppers & Potatoes
ing: 2 packs chicken sausage, sliced into thick coins
3 bell peppers (use three different colors), thick strips
1 tbsp olive oil · Italian seasoning · garlic powder

steps.t: Oven to 425°F. Potatoes cut-side down with the oil, Italian seasoning, and garlic powder. Roast 15 min alone — they need the head start.
Meanwhile slice the sausage and peppers thick. Thick, not thin — thin strips go limp and disappear.
Everything onto the pan, toss once, back in for 18 min. Pull it when the pepper edges char. Those blackened edges are where the flavor is.

recipes.note: Three colors of pepper, not three of the same. Costs the same and it is the difference between a meal you look forward to and a beige tray — which is exactly what went wrong with last week’s stir-fry.

recipes.name: Protein Mac & Cheese
ing: 1 box Kraft PowerMac (Muscle Mac works too — 20g instead of 17g)
Splash of Fairlife milk for the sauce packet

steps.t: Beef into a skillet over medium-high, break it up, cook until no pink, ~7 min. Salt it properly — the box brings the cheese, the beef has to bring the seasoning.
Make the box exactly per its directions while the beef cooks. Use milk rather than water where you have the choice.
Fold the beef through the finished mac. Three containers.

recipes.note: The box alone is 17g of protein — the beef is what takes a portion to 60g. On a night when even this is too much, the box on its own is still a legitimate 350-calorie meal; just log it as half a portion.
